item.title: OpenHuman Open Source Agent Harness Launched with Local-First Memory
item.description:
OpenHuman Open Source Agent Harness Launched with Local-First Memory

OpenHuman has launched as an open source agent harness featuring agent orchestration, workflows, and local-first memory. Within one week of its launch, the project became the number one trending repository on GitHub for nine consecutive days.

🔍 Overview

OpenHuman is described as a personal AI super intelligence that functions as a deep researcher, an orchestrator, and a brain that remembers everything. It is not AGI.

🧩 How it works

OpenHuman provides three primary capabilities:

Feature Description
Brain Builds a persistent, local memory of your world
Orchestrator Runs fleets of agents on durable graphs
Deep Researcher Sweeps data and the web before a user finishes asking

⚙️ Key details

  • Memory Tree + Obsidian Wiki: Data is compressed into scored Markdown trees in SQLite on the user’s machine and mirrored as an Obsidian vault for opening and editing.
  • Integrations: The system includes 100+ OAuth integrations, 5,000+ MCP servers, and 90,000+ Skills for one-click access to tools such as GitHub, Slack, Notion, and Gmail.
  • Auto-fetch: A feature that feeds the brain every 20 minutes to provide updated context.

🚀 Availability

Installers are available via the GitHub Releases page or at tinyhumans.ai/openhuman.

#OpenHuman #OpenSource #AIAgents #GitHub

Source: tinyhumansai/openhuman

item.title: Tracking Pull Request Performance of Top SWE Coding Agents
item.description:
Tracking Pull Request Performance of Top SWE Coding Agents

A new repository tracks the opened and merged pull requests (PRs) from top software engineering (SWE) coding agents developed by OpenAI, GitHub, and other entities.

🔍 Overview

The repository categorizes pull requests into three types:

  • All PRs: Every pull request created by an agent, including DRAFT PRs.
  • Ready PRs: Non-draft pull requests that are ready for review and merging.
  • Merged PRs: Pull requests that were successfully merged into the codebase.

⚙️ Key details

Different agents utilize different workflows for PR creation:

  • Codex: Iterates privately and creates ready PRs directly, resulting in high merge rates and few drafts.
  • Copilot and Codegen: Create draft PRs first to encourage public iteration before marking them as ready for review.

To ensure a fair comparison across these different workflows, statistics focus on Ready PRs only.

📊 Agent Statistics

Agent Ready PRs Merged PRs Merge Rate
Copilot 1,606,114 1,542,535 96.04%
Codex 6,896,711 6,179,306 89.6%
Cursor 820,725 834,966 101.74%
Devin 244,909 150,954 61.64%
Codegen 5,628 3,462 61.51%
Jules 235,475 202,177 85.86%

#SWEagents #codingagents #GitHub #OpenAI

Source: aavetis/PRarena
